questions.q: What does READ UNCOMMITTED actually do under the hood?
options: Reads that don't take shared locks for themselves and don't honor other sessions' exclusive locks either
Reads that take a shared lock and hold it for the whole transaction
Reads that automatically retry if blocked
Reads that only return rows inserted before the transaction started
questions.explain: READ UNCOMMITTED skips the locking protocol for reads entirely, which is why it can see another session's in-flight, uncommitted changes.

questions.q: Which anomalies are possible under READ UNCOMMITTED?
options: All three: dirty reads, nonrepeatable reads, and phantom reads
Only phantom reads
Only dirty reads
None -- READ UNCOMMITTED still prevents all three
questions.explain: READ UNCOMMITTED is the loosest level and the only one where all three classic anomalies can occur, including the dirty read, which no other level permits.

questions.q: What table hint produces the same effect as SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ UNCOMMITTED, scoped to one query?
options: WITH (NOLOCK)
WITH (ROWLOCK)
WITH (UPDLOCK)
WITH (TABLOCK)
questions.explain: WITH (NOLOCK) is a per-query table hint with the exact same don't-take-or-honor-locks behavior as the session-level READ UNCOMMITTED setting.

questions.q: Which anomaly is READ UNCOMMITTED uniquely responsible for allowing, compared to every other isolation level in this cluster?
options: The dirty read -- every other level prevents it completely
The phantom read -- every other level prevents it completely
The nonrepeatable read -- every other level prevents it completely
None -- all anomalies are equally possible under every level
questions.explain: READ UNCOMMITTED is the only standard isolation level where a dirty read is possible at all; READ COMMITTED and everything stricter always reads only committed data.

questions.q: What's often a better modern alternative to READ UNCOMMITTED for non-blocking reporting queries?
options: RCSI, because it gives non-blocking reads without the dirty-read risk, by reading a last-committed version instead of in-flight data
SERIALIZABLE, because it is the strictest level
There is no better alternative -- READ UNCOMMITTED is always the right choice for reporting
REPEATABLE READ, because it also avoids blocking
questions.explain: RCSI uses row versioning to give readers a non-blocking, last-committed view of the data -- the concurrency benefit of READ UNCOMMITTED without its dirty-read risk.
